content.en: Vertical ocean layers categorized by sunlight penetration, governing primary biological productivity, phytoplankton photosynthesis, and aquatic biodiversity distribution.
content.hi: Vertical ocean layers categorized by sunlight penetration, governing primary biological productivity, phytoplankton photosynthesis, and aquatic biodiversity distribution.

content.en:
• Photic (Euphotic) Zone: Extends from ocean surface down to where light intensity falls to ~1% of surface value (typically 0 to 200 meters in clear waters). Supports 90% of all marine life and all photosynthetic activity.
• Compensation Depth: Depth where photosynthetic rate equals respiratory rate (Net primary productivity = 0).
• Aphotic Zone: Region below 200m depth where sunlight cannot penetrate; sustained by marine snow (detritus drifting down from photic zone) and chemosynthesis (hydrothermal vents).

question.en: At the Compensation Depth in an aquatic ecosystem, what is the relationship between photosynthesis and respiration?
question.hi: At the Compensation Depth in an aquatic ecosystem, what is the relationship between photosynthesis and respiration?

text.en: Photosynthesis is double the rate of respiration
text.hi: Photosynthesis is double the rate of respiration

text.en: Photosynthesis rate equals respiration rate (Net Production = 0)
text.hi: Photosynthesis rate equals respiration rate (Net Production = 0)

explanation.en: At the compensation depth, light intensity is just sufficient for the rate of photosynthesis to equal the rate of respiration, meaning net primary production is zero.
